text: What brings you here today? Yeah, I have this pain in my chest. Where is the pain exactly? It's just over on the left side.
summary: The patient presents with chest pain located on the left side of the chest.

text: When did this pain start? It started just 30 minutes ago. Did it come on randomly or during activity? I was shoveling the driveway when it came on.
summary: The chest pain started suddenly 30 minutes ago while the patient was shoveling the driveway.

text: Has the pain been getting worse? The pain has been there the whole time and has gotten worse since it started.
summary: The pain has been constant and progressively worsening since onset.

text: How would you describe the pain? It feels dull, with a lot of pressure on my chest. How severe is the pain from zero to ten? Seven.
summary: The pain is described as dull and pressure-like, rated as 7 out of 10.

text: Have you had similar pain before? No, this is the first time. Does it travel anywhere? No, it stays on the left side.
summary: This is the first episode of chest pain, and it does not radiate.

text: Does anything make it worse or better? It's worse when moving or walking. It doesn't improve with anything. It's worse when lying down.
summary: The pain worsens with movement and lying down and does not improve with rest.

text: Any other symptoms like cough or difficulty breathing? I've felt short of breath since the pain started.
summary: The patient reports shortness of breath since the onset of chest pain.

text: Any recent injury? I play rugby and was tackled yesterday, but my chest felt fine afterward. Any travel or sick contacts? No.
summary: The patient reports recent physical activity but no clear trauma, travel, or infectious exposure.

text: Any nausea, vomiting, fever, or chills? No nausea or vomiting, but I feel hot. My temperature was 38 degrees.
summary: The patient reports fever of 38°C without gastrointestinal symptoms.

text: Any leg swelling, fatigue, or dizziness? No swelling, no fatigue, and no fainting. I do feel my heart beating faster.
summary: The patient reports palpitations but denies swelling, fatigue, dizziness, or syncope.

text: I have high blood pressure and high cholesterol. I take lisinopril, rosuvastatin, and a multivitamin. No allergies.
summary: The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and is on appropriate medications.

text: I live with my parents in a house and work as a city bus driver. I exercise occasionally and have a balanced diet.
summary: The patient lives with family, works as a bus driver, and maintains moderate lifestyle habits.

text: I smoke half a pack to a pack a day and have smoked for 20 years. I don't drink alcohol. I have used crystal meth, last used six days ago.
summary: The patient has significant risk factors including long-term smoking and intermittent crystal meth use.
